overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding two executive sessions (Oct. 10 and Oct. 23, 2017) on a building permit fee that did not fall under Purpose 6; no violation found on the town manager's distribution of the spreadsheet; authority question declined. Ordered future compliance; nullification declined because the vote was in open session.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board's October 23, 2017 executive session on the building permit fee for the Indian Hill Music School was not legally justified.
allegations.key_passage: Rather, the Board considered the request to reduce the building permit fee in its capacity as the issuer of the permit.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board's October 10, 2017 executive session on the building permit fee for the Indian Hill Music School was not legally justified.
allegations.key_passage: In this case, it is not related to the purchase, lease, exchange, or value of real property.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the town manager facilitated an unlawful deliberation by forwarding a Board member's spreadsheet, containing opinions, to the Board before a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the author did not intend to distribute the spreadsheet to the Board, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board lacked legal authority to approve a reduction in the building permit fee; the AG declined to review this as outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation is beyond the scope of the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance, and caution the Board that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law,
